newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end down over two percent.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end down over two percent.

text.p: Swiss shares ended near session lows on Wednesday, losing more than two percent in broad declines tied to selling in index futures, traders said.
"We saw a lot of pressure from the SMI (Swiss Market Index) future," one dealer said, adding U.S. economic data were basically favourable, but did not improve Swiss sentiment.
The market was expected to remain volatile before U.S. consumer prices and jobless claims on Thursday and the expiry of Swiss options and futures on Friday.
The blue-chip SMI slid 126.3 points, or 2.17 percent to 5,682.1 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 72.40 points, or 1.95 percent, at 3,640.95.
Bourse volume was fairly heavy at 3.3 billion Swiss francs.
Swiss Bank Corp resisted declines for much of the day, but ended down two francs at 415.
SBC's group net profit rose 84 percent in the first half, well above analysts' forecasts for a rise of 50 to 70 percent.
"SBC was the only major Swiss bank which exceeded the market's expectations," one trader said.
SBC was also seen profiting from switches out of other banks. Credit Suisse Group and Winterthur, which announced merger plans on Monday, continued to fall.

CS Group was down 13.25 franc at 190.25. Winterthur lost 88 francs to 1,416. One dealer said the sentiment for the two stocks was still poor. Analysts have expressed some reservations about the cost and timing of the merger.
Novartis registereds led the actives list, falling 36 francs to 2,279. Roche fell 370 francs to 13,770.
Swiss Life, which jumped 12 percent on Tuesday, rose 64 francs to 985. Dealers speculated that Swiss banks may be buying the stock.

On the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex) a total of 178,379 options were traded. Dealers said that trading in UBS calls alone accounted for 61,000 of the volume. On the futures side, 16,703 SMI futures changed hands. About half of them were August futures, which ended down 140 points at 5,670.
